items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: there were some members left from that band that you played with... Hayes Pillars and Charles Pillars.

ctx.x: So, for the record, we’ll state that contrary to what’s been written you never played with Alphonso Trent’s band but there were some members left from that band that you played with.
Right, trombone player named Snub Mosely and Chester Clark, trumpet player, alto player named Lee Hilliard and James Jeter, and Hayes Pillars and Charles Pillars.
Was Snub Mosely playing his slide saxophone even then?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: So the Jeter-Pillars was the one --, Jeter was an alto saxophone player and Pillars was a tenor player... So he came to Jeter-Pillars in between? Yeah... So we got Walter Page.

ctx.x: Stuff Smith was in that band, yeah. Snuff Smith was in that band. Alphonso Trent, he got sick up in Bangor, Maine, up there, they were doing one-nighters. So he went back to Ft. Smith, Arkansas. So the band came through Columbus, Ohio and broke up. So the Jeter-Pillars was the one --, Jeter was an alto saxophone player and Pillars was a tenor player. They decided they would get the band going, you know.
They were both in Trent's band, I see.
